- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the immediate next period; apply a 5–10% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if price deviates >10% from recent 7-day average, adjust forecast toward that mean, especially if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward trends in sentiment-heavy periods; add 2–5% buffer if sentiment >0.70 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often misses the pivot; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% to capture momentum shift.
